analysis: Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, a documentation-only change with no executable code, config or protocol changes. The patch excerpt shows: a date bump, a note that video_url input supports constant or variable frame rate, a startup warning about GLM-5.3-Flash GPU wired-memory limits, status output text, and a new doctor 'glm wired limit' check section (head lines ~1100-1130). I checked these against the threat model. The GLM wired-limit advice is advisory only; the doc states it does not change admission, KV grants or capacity. It matches error text without logging it, so there is no new prompt or content exposure. It prints a copy-paste `sudo tee` / `launchctl bootstrap system` LaunchDaemon install for the operator. That is an operator-run instruction with fixed sysctl values, not new code or privileged helper surface, so it does not affect TB-010 or T-044/T-045. The variable-frame-rate video note touches the media path (T-050, inline video plaintext in temp files), but the excerpt only states supported input types. The T-050 temp-file mitigation cannot be verified from this docs diff, so I have no evidence of a regression. The existing logout/revocation, drain and Autopilot documentation (A-008, TB-011, T-053) appears unchanged in the patch ranges; the changed ranges are only lines 3, 52, 178-180, 949-952 and 1100-1130. The logout text describes bearer-token revocation with a recorded issuer, no redirects and HTTP 204 confirmation, which is consistent with the threat-model header. No security regression, invalidated assumption or threat-model gap is identified. Remaining integration question: whether the underlying source changes (GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice, GLMWiredLimitAdvice, VFR video decode) exist in other batches and keep decrypted video out of temp files. They are not visible here.
